tickets.recommended_action: Rotating equipment specialist to diagnose NDE vibration and set operating/repair disposition; correct per findings, verify vibration against approved limits, and trend daily. Obtain source-required attention today. Verify current trend, limits and repair status.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: For the train's gas-export compression function, vibration more than doubled over six weeks and continues rising, supporting strong progression. It remains below alarm; neither imminent failure nor lost compression capability is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of gas-export compression would send the platform to recycle and cut production within an hour, with no spare or workaround. This supports a material operational consequence; extreme loss or a specific severe personnel consequence is not established.

tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer: check regulatory deadline/two-year test status, diagnose passing, approve operating/repair disposition; repair if confirmed. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. After repair, test set pressure/tightness. Gas-test area; verify personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Audible hissing and hydrocarbon smell below set pressure support active suspected passing, a meaningful precursor to loss of reliable overpressure protection. They do not demonstrate inability to relieve at the required pressure or capacity.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure would remove the listed nonredundant overpressure protection of the first-stage production separator, creating a specific pressure-boundary failure and hydrocarbon-release path. Extreme consequence scale is not established; exposure and other safeguards remain unverified.

tickets.summary: FW-8102 failed first start, then started on attempt 2 after ~8 s cranking and reached rated pressure; batteries were 22.8 V at rest. On-demand firewater reliability is impaired; partner A later delivered 9.2 vs 11 barg, leaving backup capacity unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Mechanical engineer to disposition and repair starting-system faults found. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test batteries/charger and starting air. Prove first-start and rated pressure. Verify A pressure/flow against duty.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is FW-8102 starting on demand to supply firewater. Its first-attempt failure during the 3 June test confirms an interruption of that function. Second-attempt starting after about eight seconds of cranking, followed by normal running at rated discharge pressure, bounds the failure but does not erase it. The 22.8 V measurement was at rest, not during cranking; battery causation is unconfirmed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure to start removes this pump's on-demand firewater contribution, degrading fire protection. The explicitly linked partner started first time on 17 June but delivered 9.2 barg against 11 barg design, with flow unmeasured; fully capable redundancy cannot be credited. This supports a severe protection-loss consequence, not confirmed total firewater loss or extreme consequences. Both-pump unavailability would require production shutdown, but that combined state is not established.

tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to set operating/repair disposition; repair confirmed wall loss and insulation water ingress; verify thickness >=7.4 mm and pressure integrity. Map wall loss and confirm current condition. Check personnel exposure and release controls.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is pressure containment by PL-1002. impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this six-inch production flowline could release hydrocarbons at full wellhead pressure, providing a specific severe release/ignition consequence path. No redundant line is identified. Personnel exposure, isolation effectiveness and release scale remain unknown; extreme consequences are not established.

tickets.summary: FG-0455 failed to detect 50% LEL gas on both cylinder attempts, degrading compression-module gas protection; the other two heads responded, retaining 2oo3 capability but losing its failure margin.
tickets.recommended_action: Instrument engineer to diagnose head/circuit, repair or replace as indicated; verify response to 50% LEL gas and voted outputs. Check impairment/deviation register. Verify current group status and restoration.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is this detector head's hydrocarbon-gas detection, not the entire voted group. impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of this head materially degrades hydrocarbon-gas protection in the compression module. Both remaining heads responded correctly, supporting retained voted capability at the observation, rather than total protection defeat. Loss of failure margin supports moderate impact, not an extreme major-accident consequence attributed to this single failure.

tickets.summary: CR-5001's poorly lubricated hoist rope has 6 broken wires/lay versus 10 discard at the max-radius drum section; load support is degraded, not proven lost. Failure risks dropped loads and stops offloads, affecting logistics within days.
tickets.recommended_action: Lubricate rope; obtain lifting engineer/surveyor disposition under lifting standard, including repair need and inspection cadence; verify post-correction condition against 10-wire/lay discard criterion. Reinspect rope extent and trend. Check lift loads, heights and exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is main-hoist load support and lifting. Six broken wires per lay versus a discard criterion of ten establishes limited degradation with remaining criterion margin. Poor lubrication warrants correction, but no progression trend or operational loss is established.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Main-hoist failure could release a suspended load and cause personnel injury. Crane unavailability also prevents supply-boat offloads, creating logistics problems within days, with no redundant crane recorded. These support material consequences; load, height and personnel exposure are insufficiently defined to support a severe consequence band.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is maintaining the required temporary-refuge envelope pressure. tickets.summary: DEL-8300 lost fire-control coverage at ~12/60 north-quadrant nozzles above two producing wellheads despite normal header conditions. A later closed valve was reopened after an unknown duration; nozzle restoration remains unverified.
tickets.recommended_action: Fire-protection engineer: inspect branches/nozzles, clear blockage as found; approve repair/operating plan. Verify nozzle impairment/deviation record. Flow-test all nozzles for required coverage. Verify current protection control alignment. Check wellhead fire/personnel exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery of effective deluge coverage through the north-quadrant nozzles. The full-flow test demonstrated absent or badly distorted delivery at approximately 12 of 60 nozzles, confirming partial required-function loss, not total system failure. The later valve reopening does not demonstrate restoration of this delivery function.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of deluge coverage directly above two producing wellheads compromises local fire control and supports a severe fire-escalation consequence path. No redundant arrangement is listed. This does not establish total deluge loss or an extreme consequence; actual personnel exposure and remaining effective coverage require verification.

tickets.recommended_action: Instrument/control engineer to assess operating disposition, diagnose and recalibrate/repair as indicated. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Test accuracy, control and alarm to spec. Validate both legs and sight glass. Check level-upset consequences and exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is reliable interface-level measurement for V-1201 control and high-level alarm. Divergence from two references grew steadily over about three weeks, supporting strong progression. Absolute accuracy and acceptance tolerance remain unverified; the backup's later flat line does not establish failure of this transmitter.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of reliable measurement affects separator control and the high-level alarm, supporting a material operational consequence. Backup capability cannot be credited: on 18 June it was reported flat for approximately 36 hours, with blockage or sensor failure suspected. No specific severe accident or personnel-exposure path is established.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Assessed function is inlet-flow deflection for test separation. impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of inlet deflection would affect the local test-separation function. The vessel is reported out of service, its shell and heads are sound, and it can remain isolated and bypassed without production impact. tickets.summary: V-2450's dirty gauge glass limits independent level checking, but control appears normal with no carryover indications; loss of scrubber liquid removal could damage turbines.
tickets.recommended_action: Safely isolate as required, clean and inspect the gauge glass; repair any defects found under approved maintenance procedures. Verify readability and level agreement.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Assessed function: V-2450 removal of liquid from turbine fuel gas. Dirty gauge glass limits local level checking, but transmitter-based control appears normal and no downstream carryover indications were observed. This supports little indication of near-term separation-function loss, not proof of full capability. The history contains only the 16 June observation and no restoration record.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of the scrubber's liquid-removal function could deliver a liquid slug to the turbines and cause material equipment damage. No scrubber redundancy is listed. This supports a material operational consequence, but not a specific severe personnel or major-accident consequence. The score concerns scrubber function loss, not the cost of cleaning its glass.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Failure of this nonredundant valve would remove compressor-discharge overpressure protection, creating a specific pressure-integrity threat. tickets.summary: FW-8101 produced 9.2 vs 11 barg design with flow unmeasured, raising doubt about firewater delivery despite starting normally; FW-8102's earlier failed first start limits redundancy confidence, with shutdown if both become unavailable.
tickets.recommended_action: Mechanical/fire engineer: correct verified faults, set operating disposition and retain weekly tests. Verify impairment and deviation status. Retest pressure/flow to approved 11-barg duty. Inspect test valves and pump internals. Verify FW-8102 on-demand capability.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is delivery of required firewater pressure and flow by pump A. Running pressure below design is a meaningful performance precursor, but unmeasured flow and missing acceptance criteria prevent confirmation of required-function loss. Normal first-time starting and engine parameters do not establish delivery capability. Internal wear and a partly closed test-line valve remain alternative suspected causes; progression is unknown.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of required firewater delivery would degrade fire suppression and expose personnel and plant to fire escalation. The explicit partner cannot receive full redundancy credit: on 3 June it failed its first start, started on the second attempt after about eight seconds of cranking, then ran normally and achieved rated discharge pressure. This does not establish present unavailability or a shared delivery defect. Both pumps unavailable would require production shutdown; neither that condition nor extreme consequences are established.

tickets.recommended_action: Fire-protection engineer: inspect cause, restore tag; approve repair/operating disposition. Verify current protection control alignment. Reconcile impairment/deviation record. Witness function test; close impairment only after pass. Trace closure duration and fire exposure.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: The assessed function is admitting deluge water through the north-quadrant branch isolation valve. Its chained-closed position establishes an actual loss of that function. Immediate reopening is confirmed, but restored delivery is not verified; this score describes the observed failure, not a claim that the valve remains closed.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of branch supply removes deluge coverage above two producing wellheads, providing a specific fire-escalation and personnel-harm pathway. No redundant arrangement is listed. This supports severe consequences, but not an extreme installation-wide outcome.

tickets.summary: Damp insulation and rust staining at V-1201's manway suggest hidden corrosion of the first-stage pressure boundary; wall condition is unknown, and containment failure could release production hydrocarbons.
tickets.recommended_action: Integrity engineer to direct repair/operating disposition; correct ingress and renew insulation after repair. Check impairment/deviation register. Expose manway area; UT-map against limits. Check pressure, inventory and exposure. Verify repaired containment to approved limits.

likelihood_of_failure.rationale: Wet insulation and rust staining provide a meaningful precursor to hidden corrosion, but neither wall loss nor its progression is measured. The historically thick-walled vessel does not establish current margin. Linked piping, relief-valve and transmitter observations do not establish vessel damage.

impact_of_failure.rationale: Loss of the pressure boundary of the entire first-stage production separator provides a specific severe hydrocarbon-release path, with no redundant vessel listed. This is not a consequence of insulation repair. Inventory, pressure and personnel exposure remain unknown, so extreme consequences are not established.
